reason: I ran archive.org full-text search myself. Soul Food: Nourishing Poems for Starved Minds (Bloodaxe, 2007) prints Triumph of being, headed EDITH SODERGRAN, translated from the Finland Swedish by DAVID McDUFF, running: What have I to fear? I am a part of infinity, / I am a part of the all’s great power, / a lonely world within millions of worlds, / ... degree that fades last. / Triumph of living, triumph of breathing, triumph of being! That is the card's wording to the letter, and it stands fifth, after four lines ending that fades last, so line 5 holds. The same search shows other translators render it differently (Katchadourian, Love and Solitude, 1992: The triumph of living, the triumph of breathing, the triumph of existing!), so this is McDuff's rendering and not drift into another. The Swedish (Triumf att leva, triumf att andas, triumf att finnas till!) is from Septemberlyran (1918), which fits. shipped.js: not shipped, Södergran at 0 of 3, not banned. In scope, publishable, and the line the poem is named for, so it is the sentence the work is known by. Source about 92 characters, leads with the name, no dash, tag Poetry. Soft point: the wording was read in a 2007 Bloodaxe anthology, which probably reprints McDuff from the revised Complete Poems of 1992 rather than the 1984 first edition the source names; I could not open either edition, and a difference, if any, is unlikely to touch this line.
